title: Fruitcake Canna-Cocktail: A Holiday THC Mocktail
h1: A Fruitcake-Spiced Canna-Cocktail Without the Booze
metaDescription: A holiday THC mocktail of chilled black tea, cranberry and berry preserves, with orange peel, warm fruitcake spices and a measured tincture. No liquor.
excerpt: Black tea, cranberry and berry preserves with orange peel and warm spice: an alcohol-free holiday glass with a measured THC tincture shaken in.
keyTakeaways: Chilled black tea, cranberry juice and cherry or blueberry preserves bring fruitcake's dark-fruit depth.
Read the tincture label, start low, and shake the dose in before the ice so it mixes through.
It's alcohol-free by design; top it with berry seltzer for a sparkling version.
Mix the same base without tincture so every guest gets a festive glass.
body:
This holiday THC mocktail earns its fruitcake name. It starts as a black tea mocktail, with cranberry juice and berry preserves for dark-fruit depth. Orange peel and a pinch of warm spice add the bakery notes, and a measured THC tincture is shaken right in. There's no liquor, just a festive glass that tastes like the holidays.

## Start with the label

The dose comes from the tincture, so read its label first: it lists THC in mg per ml. Measure with the marked dropper or a small oral syringe, and start low. Health Canada suggests new consumers begin at 2.5 mg of THC or less. Shake the tincture with the tea, juice and preserves before any ice goes in, so it mixes through the whole drink. Then give it at least 2 hours before a second glass. Our [cannabis tincture guide](/blog/cannabis-tincture-guide/) and [THC dosage guide](/blog/thc-dosage-guide/) go deeper.

## The fruitcake flavors

Fruitcake means candied peel, dark fruit and warm spice, so the glass leans on the same notes:

- **Black tea**, regular or decaf, for a malty backbone
- **Cranberry juice** for tart fruit
- **Cherry or blueberry preserves** for jammy sweetness
- **Orange peel** and a pinch of cinnamon, allspice or nutmeg
- **Dried or maraschino cherries** to garnish

## Shake, strain, serve your holiday THC mocktail

Shake everything with the tincture until the preserves dissolve, add ice and shake again, then strain over fresh ice. Twist the orange peel over the glass and drop it in with the cherries. For a sparkling version, strain into a tall glass and top with berry seltzer.

## Batching and labeling

Mix to order when you can, so each glass gets its own measured dose. If you batch a pitcher, stir the total tincture dose in thoroughly, label the pitcher 'contains THC' with the dose per cup, and serve it with a measuring cup. Pour out whatever remains once the party winds down instead of saving it, and keep tinctures away from children and pets. If someone drinks an infused glass by accident, call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222.

## A zero-THC glass for everyone else

Make the same base without tincture in a second, clearly marked pitcher, so every guest gets the fruitcake glass. Keep the infused version for adults 21+ who know what's in it, and make sure nobody who drinks it drives. For more seasonal ideas, see our [holiday infused recipes](/blog/holiday-cannabis-infused-recipes/), the [pineapple-grapefruit THC sparkler](/blog/pineapple-grapefruit-thc-sparkler/) and our [infused apple cider](/blog/lifted-bright-apple-cider/).

Stocking up for holiday hosting? Browse your nearest High Society store's [menu](/shop/) and order ahead for curbside pickup. Members of The Society, our free loyalty program, earn points on qualifying purchases. Please consume responsibly.

faq.q: How much tincture goes in one mocktail?
faq.a: Enough for the dose you chose, measured in milliliters. Multiply the ml you add by the label's mg per ml: 1 ml of a tincture labeled 3 mg per ml is about 3 mg, for example. Keep the first glass small, and wait at least 2 hours before deciding on another.

Yes. Decaf black tea keeps the same malty backbone with only a trace of caffeine, which makes the glass easier to enjoy late in the evening. Brew it strong, since ice and juice dilute it, and chill it completely before mixing. Rooibos works too, for a naturally caffeine-free glass with a warm, slightly sweet flavor.

faq.q: Does caffeine change how THC feels?
faq.a: It might, and there's no reliable way to predict how it will for you. Caffeine is a stimulant, and THC affects people differently, so the pairing can feel different from one person to the next. To keep things simple, brew decaf, so the THC you measured is the one new variable in your glass.

ingredients: 4 ounces strong black tea, regular or decaf, brewed and chilled
1 small pinch of cinnamon, allspice or nutmeg
THC tincture, measured for 1 serving (see the dosing note)
steps: Combine the tea, cranberry juice, preserves, spice and measured tincture in a cocktail shaker or a jar with a tight lid.
Shake hard for about 10 seconds, until the preserves have dissolved.
Add a handful of ice and shake for another 10 seconds.
Strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice. Twist the orange peel over the drink, then drop it in with the cherries.
For a sparkling version, strain into a tall glass of ice instead and top with berry seltzer.
recipe.dosingNote: **One glass, one measured dose:** ml of tincture × the label's mg per ml = THC in the drink. Example: 1 ml of a tincture labeled 3 mg per ml is about 3 mg. A homemade tincture is an estimate that depends on the flower's potency and on decarboxylation and extraction losses. Start low, wait at least 2 hours before a second, label any batched pitcher, and keep infused drinks away from children and pets.

review.summary: 19 claims checked: 17 ok, 2 overstated (2 fixed). No liquor anywhere; rewards line matches hs-facts with no point values.

claims.claim: Health Canada suggests new consumers begin at 2.5 mg of THC or less
claims.source: https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/drugs-medication/cannabis/resources/what-you-need-to-know-if-you-choose-to-consume-cannabis.html (WebFetch): 'if you are a new consumer, look for a product containing 2.5 mg of THC or less.'

claims.claim: The tincture label lists THC in mg per ml; measure with the marked dropper or an oral syringe
claims.source: facts/law-facts.json mi-labeling: Michigan products are labeled with their THC and CBD content

claims.claim: Shake the tincture with the tea, juice and preserves before the ice so it mixes through
claims.source: https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/16078 (PubChem REST API): THC 'Essentially insoluble in water', so mixing before the ice dilutes and chills it is reasoning, no figure

claims.claim: Give it at least 2 hours before a second glass; keep the first glass small
claims.source: https://www.cdc.gov/cannabis/faq/index.html (WebFetch): 'it can take up to 2 hours to feel the effects from the drug.'

claims.claim: Tincture math: 1 ml of a 3 mg/ml tincture is about 3 mg
A homemade tincture is an estimate that depends on flower potency and decarboxylation and extraction losses
claims.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5549281/ (Wang 2016, full text via Europe PMC REST): 'the conversion of the acid to Δ9-THC was never perfectly complete without loss or degradation of starting material'

claims.claim: Fruitcake means candied peel, dark fruit and warm spice; black tea gives a malty backbone; cranberry and cherry or blueberry preserves bring dark-fruit depth
claims.source: flavor description, no figure; brief angle (orange peel, warm spice, dried cherry make the name honest)

claims.claim: Mix to order 'since it keeps every dose exact'
claims.fix: now 'so each glass gets its own measured dose': a per-glass measure avoids pitcher error, but no homemade or labeled figure is exact
claims.source: the article's own dosing note (homemade tincture is an estimate); facts/law-facts.json mi-labeling details (label values carry a stated variance)

claims.claim: A batched pitcher gets stirred thoroughly, a 'contains THC' label with the dose per cup and a measuring cup; leftovers are poured out
claims.source: brief outline (batched pitcher gets an 'infused' label; mix to order); guidance, no figure

claims.claim: If someone drinks an infused glass by accident, call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222; keep tinctures away from children and pets
claims.source: https://www.cdc.gov/cannabis/faq/index.html: 'call a poison control center at: at 1-800-222-1222.'; Health Canada page above: store edible cannabis 'out of reach of children, youth, and pets.'

claims.claim: Keep the infused version for adults 21+ who know what's in it, and make sure nobody who drinks it drives
claims.source: facts/law-facts.json mi-au-age (21+) and mi-au-impaired-driving (Michigan bans driving while under the influence)

claims.claim: Decaf black tea keeps the malty backbone 'without the caffeine'
claims.fix: now 'with only a trace of caffeine': decaffeinated black tea still carries a little caffeine
claims.source: USDA FoodData Central (api.nal.usda.gov, SR Legacy), fdcId 174871 'Beverages, tea, black, brewed, prepared with tap water, decaffeinated': caffeine 1.0 mg per 100 g, against 20.0 mg per 100 g for regular brewed black tea (fdcId 173227)

claims.claim: Rooibos works too, for a naturally caffeine-free glass
claims.source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42615889/ (Food Addit Contam Part A, 2026, abstract via E-utilities): 'Rooibos is a naturally caffeine-free herbal tea'

claims.claim: Caffeine is a stimulant; there's no reliable way to predict how caffeine and THC will feel together; brew decaf to keep it simple
claims.source: no research claim made (the writer recorded finding no human study of the combination); caffeine's stimulant role is general knowledge

claims.claim: Brew the tea strong, since ice and juice dilute it; shake about 10 seconds until the preserves dissolve, then with ice
claims.source: ordinary drink technique with visual cues; no figure

claims.claim: No liquor: alcohol-free by design, berry seltzer for a sparkling version
claims.source: read of the ingredients and steps (brief mustAvoid: adding liquor)

review.notes: Independent fact-check, 2026-10-24. Health Canada and the CDC FAQ reopened with WebFetch; decaf tea caffeine read from USDA FoodData Central's API (mayoclinic.org returned 403); rooibos checked through an E-utilities abstract. The caffeine-and-THC FAQ makes no research claim, so none was needed. Sources list kept: both are https and support the text. High Society: one paragraph at the end (menu, curbside, The Society), all in hs-facts, away from any effect copy. Writer's notes: No liquor (brief mustAvoid). Fruitcake flavors (orange peel, warm spice, dried cherry) make the name honest, per the brief notes. High Society mentioned once (menu, curbside pickup; The Society as free and earning points on qualifying purchases, hs-facts rewards.howToJoin and rewards.earning; no point values, tiers or deal terms).
